title: Responsive table virtualization and modal gesture handling for Console dashboards & cost views
creator: Priya Singh
description: Goal: Improve resilience and perceptual performance of Console pages that render dense tables and chart panels, and ensure modals behave consistently across browsers and input modes (mouse, touch, trackpad, keyboard). Scope: - Virtualize long tables (billing rows, per-token cost tables) so initial paint is fast on low-end laptops and mobile. - Implement sticky header + sticky first column behavior with correct z-index and focus order. - Design modal stacking and drag/gesture handling for touch devices; ensure scroll anchoring when modals open/close. - Fallbacks for canvas-based charts: defer canvas draw when offscreen, ensure ARIA labels and non-canvas fallbacks for accessibility tests. Out of scope: server-side pagination changes, deep changes to backend pagination API.
acceptance_criteria: Tables with >200 rows render initial viewport within 200ms on a 3-year-old MacBook Air
Sticky header/column remains aligned with virtualization during fast scroll and window resize
Modals on mobile use drag-to-dismiss gesture; dismiss animation preserves scroll anchoring of the underlying page
Cross-browser verified in latest stable Chrome, Safari, Firefox and iOS Safari; documented workarounds for legacy Edge if any
Keyboard navigation preserves focus order when virtual rows mount/unmount; passes automated a11y checks (axe-core)

decisions: Use virtualization windowing with a small buffer (6 rows) and a 120ms unmount debounce to handle momentum scroll in Safari
Implement sticky header + sticky first column using CSS where supported; fallback to JS positioning for browsers with known bugs
Modal behavior: on touch devices enable drag-to-dismiss; on desktop enable ESC and click-outside; preserve page scroll position via ENG-anchored-scroll API
